P0C00.d: P0C00 reports that the current of drive motor A is lower than the controller expects for the commanded torque, the counterpart of P0C01 (current high). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM and Stellantis use only P0C01 from this group.
s: Weak or missing electric drive torque
Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Vehicle runs on the engine only or in limp mode
c: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection at motor A or the inverter
Inverter power stage for motor A not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor A

P0C01.d: P0C01 is the overcurrent check of drive motor A, meant to protect the inverter's IGBTs. GM sets it when any phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt, 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 tables, or 396 A on eAssist; since 2016 a too negative d-axis current (about -540 to -310 A, depending on stator temperature) also counts.
s: Limp mode with warning lamp
Reduced propulsion or engine unavailable message
Rough running or loud noise from the motor generator
c: Damaged or improperly torqued three-phase cable joints (Stellantis S2608000006)
Damaged stator winding of motor A (GM PIP5246)
Failing power switch or current measurement in the inverter

P0C02.d: P0C02 is the general current code for drive motor B, the second electric machine, such as the second motor of a two-motor hybrid or the rear motor of an electric all-wheel-drive system. It applies to a current fault that is neither classed as low (P0C03) nor high (P0C04).
s: Hybrid or electric drive warning lamp
Reduced power or loss of all-wheel drive
Limp mode
c: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase connection of motor B
Fault in the motor B inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor B

P0C03.d: P0C03 indicates that drive motor B draws less current than the controller expects for the requested torque. It is the low counterpart of P0C04 and the motor B twin of P0C00.
s: Weak or missing torque from motor B
Warning lamp for the hybrid or electric drive
Reduced performance or limp mode
c: High-resistance or loose three-phase connection of motor B
Inverter power stage for motor B not delivering current
Open or damaged winding in drive motor B

P0C04.d: P0C04 is the overcurrent check of drive motor B and protects the IGBTs of its inverter. GM flags it when the highest phase current exceeds 725 A on the 2011 Volt or 600 A on the 2012 two-mode trucks and in the 2016 to 2019 hybrid tables; the newer tables also fail a d-axis current below a stator-temperature curve of roughly -556 to -315 A.
s: Limp mode with red wrench or malfunction lamp
Sudden loss of electric drive power
c: Cross-threaded or loose three-phase cable bolts with metal debris (Stellantis S2608000006)
Shorted or damaged stator winding of motor B
Failing power switch or current measurement in the motor B inverter

P0C05.d: P0C05 detects an open or missing phase between the inverter and drive motor A. GM checks each phase as the rotor passes its axis: if the peak phase axis current stays below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees of that axis and over 35 V on the inverter, about 200 failed samples set the code.
s: Propulsion system performance message or warning lamp
Reduced electric drive power
Loss of 12 V charging or noise from the motor generator on mild hybrids
c: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor A
Software fault, cured by update (Jeep TSB 08-144-23)
Internal fault of the motor generator unit or open stator winding
One-off event that does not return after clearing (Volvo TJ 36863)

P0C06.d: P0C06 belongs to the phase circuit group of drive motor A and reports that a U, V or W phase line sits too low, typically a short to the negative high-voltage rail or to chassis ground. P0C05 covers an open or missing phase, P0C07 the opposite high state.
s: Electric drive shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time
c: Phase cable or winding shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing

P0C07.d: P0C07 is the high member of the drive motor A phase circuit group: a U, V or W phase line reads higher than it should, most likely through a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a power switch that stays on. Its siblings are P0C05 for an open phase and P0C06 for a phase pulled low.
s: Immediate shutdown of electric drive with warning lamp
Reduced performance or engine-only operation
c: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor A inverter
Phase cable shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on

P0C08.d: P0C08 is the open-phase check for drive motor B, the motor B twin of P0C05. GM runs it on the 2011 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks: each phase is checked as the rotor passes its axis, and a phase axis current below 9 A while at least 23 A is commanded, with the rotor within 30 degrees and over 35 V on the inverter, counts as a miss.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion power
Engine running more often than usual
c: Loose or open three-phase terminal between inverter and motor B
Open stator winding in drive motor B
Inverter stage for motor B not conducting

P0C09.d: P0C09 marks a U, V or W phase line of drive motor B that is pulled low, for example by a short to the negative high-voltage rail, to ground or by a power switch that conducts when it should not. It is the motor B twin of P0C06; the siblings P0C08 and P0C0A cover an open phase and a phase stuck high.
s: Motor B shut down with warning lamp
Overcurrent or insulation codes stored at the same time
c: Phase cable or winding of motor B shorted to ground or housing
Shorted low-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Insulation damage from heat, moisture or chafing

P0C0A.d: P0C0A reports that a phase line of drive motor B reads too high, typically a short to the positive high-voltage rail or a high-side power switch that stays on. It mirrors P0C07 for motor A and completes the motor B trio with P0C08 (open) and P0C09 (low).
s: Immediate shutdown of motor B with warning lamp
Reduced performance or loss of electric all-wheel drive
c: Shorted high-side power switch in the motor B inverter
Phase cable of motor B shorted to the positive high-voltage path
Faulty gate driver holding a switch on

P0C0B.d: P0C0B flags a lost or interrupted supply inside the motor A inverter. GM reads it from the IGBT module status: when the gate drive supply falls below its threshold, the module reports a bias fault; on eAssist the 5 V rail below 3.5 to 4.3 V or the 15 V rail below 10.4 to 12.6 V counts, with run/crank above 7 V.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Electric drive or motor generator unavailable
Engine cannot be started, only electric driving possible (Mercedes P3 hybrids)
c: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor A inverter
Low 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground to the inverter control board
Open high-voltage feed to the inverter, e.g. in a belt starter-alternator (Mercedes LI15.40-P-077947)

P0C0C.d: P0C0C reports that the supply voltage of the motor A inverter is present but too low, while P0C0B covers a lost or open supply and P0C0D a supply that is too high. Which supply is meant depends on the maker: GM ties its sibling P0C0B to the gate-drive supply of the IGBTs, Mercedes to the high-voltage feed.
s: Red high-voltage system warning asking to stop safely
Loss of drive power or vehicle will not get ready to drive
c: Internal fault of the drive power electronics (Audi TSB 2081725)
Weak 12 V supply, poor ground or high-resistance connector at the inverter
Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output

P0C0D.d: P0C0D reports that the supply of the motor A inverter is above its permitted range, while P0C0B stands for a lost or open supply and P0C0C for a supply that is too low. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced or no electric propulsion from motor A
Engine runs more often or the vehicle enters limp mode
c: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor A inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or a charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness

P0C0E.d: P0C0E is the motor B counterpart of P0C0B: the inverter for the second motor has lost the supply of its gate-drive board. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion message, motor B unavailable
Engine runs continuously instead of electric driving
c: Failed gate-drive power supply inside the motor B inverter
Weak 12 V feed, blown fuse or poor ground at the inverter control board
Loose or corroded low-voltage connector at the power inverter module

P0C0F.d: P0C0F means the supply of the motor B inverter is present but below its permitted range. P0C0E covers a lost or open supply, P0C10 a supply that is too high, and P0C0C is the same fault on motor A.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced propulsion, motor B unavailable
Fault appears mainly with low 12 V voltage, e.g. after standing
c: Weak 12 V battery or DC/DC converter output feeding the inverter electronics
Corroded connector or poor ground raising resistance in the inverter supply
Failing internal gate-drive power supply in the motor B inverter

P0C10.d: P0C10 flags a supply of the motor B inverter that is above its permitted range. Its siblings are P0C0E for a lost or open supply and P0C0F for a low one; P0C0D is the motor A version.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, hybrid system warning
Reduced propulsion, motor B unavailable
Vehicle limited to engine or reduced-power operation
c: Faulty voltage regulation of the gate-drive supply inside the motor B inverter
Excessive 12 V system voltage from the DC/DC converter or an external charger
Supply or sense line shorted to a higher voltage in the harness

P0C11.d: P0C11 is a protective code: the temperature sensor at phase U of the motor A inverter reads a valid but excessive value. GM uses it across its hybrids.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, often with a hybrid system overheat message
Reduced propulsion power until the inverter cools down
Electric drive unavailable, engine runs continuously
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed or weak electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged power electronics radiator or inoperative cooling fan
Sustained heavy load such as towing uphill in high ambient heat

P0C12.d: P0C12 sets when the inverter for motor A measures an excessive temperature at phase V while its sensor itself is plausible. In GM's 2011 Volt table that is PIM sensor C above 98 °C; the two-mode trucks of 2012 use 88 °C with an 85 °C reset, the 2016 Volt 126 °C for 1.2 s out of 2 s and the 2016 ELR 102.5 °C, all Type A, one trip.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Propulsion power reduced, especially under load or in hot weather
Hybrid system overheat or service message
c: Low coolant level or trapped air in the inverter cooling loop
Inoperative electric coolant pump of the power electronics
Blocked low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Degraded thermal contact or failing power stage inside the inverter

P0C13.d: P0C13 covers phase W of the motor A inverter: the controller sees a credible sensor reading that exceeds the overtemperature limit. GM's 2011 Volt uses PIM sensor E with 98 °C, the 2012 two-mode trucks 88 °C, the 2016 and 2018 tables 126 °C for 1.2 s within a 2 s window and the 2019 table 128 °C for 1.5 s, always Type A, one trip, so the MIL comes on at once.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp immediately after the fault
Reduced propulsion until temperatures drop
Engine runs more often, little or no electric driving
c: Coolant loss or air pocket in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump for the inverter stopped or running slow
Debris on the low-temperature radiator or cooling fan not running

P0C14.d: P0C14 is the motor B counterpart of P0C11: phase U of the second inverter has become too hot while its temperature sensor reads plausibly. GM documents it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion power, especially under load
Hybrid system overheat message
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics cooling loop
Failed electric coolant pump of the inverter loop
Clogged low-temperature radiator or failed cooling fan
Long periods of high load on motor B, e.g. towing or steep climbs

P0C15.d: P0C15 reports overtemperature at phase V of the motor B inverter, based on a sensor reading that is valid but above the limit. GM applies it on the Volt and the two-mode trucks: PIM sensor D above 98 °C on the 2011 Volt, 88 °C on the 2012 trucks, 102.5 °C on the 2016 ELR, 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s on the 2016 Volt and in the 2018 table, every time Type A with one trip.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion until the inverter has cooled
Engine runs more often than usual
c: Coolant loss or air in the inverter cooling loop
Electric coolant pump of the power electronics not working
Blocked radiator for the power electronics or fan failure
Poor heat transfer or ageing power stage inside the inverter

P0C16.d: P0C16 is set by the motor B inverter when phase W runs too hot and the temperature sensor itself shows no fault. GM's tables give PIM sensor F above 98 °C for the 2011 Volt, above 88 °C with an 85 °C reset for the 2012 two-mode trucks, and 131 °C for 1.2 s within 2 s for the 2016 Volt, with 1.5 s in the 2019 table; each is Type A, one trip.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after one drive
Reduced propulsion, notably at high load or high ambient temperature
Hybrid system overheat message
c: Low coolant level or air in the power electronics loop
Electric coolant pump of the inverter failed or blocked
Dirty low-temperature radiator or inoperative fan

P0C17.d: P0C17 means the controller has no valid learned offset for the resolver of motor A, which it needs to align rotor position with the stator field. GM runs the learn at key-off and sets the code if it fails without a stored value: motor speed above 50 rpm, DC voltage below 192 V (200 V on the 2016 Volt), phase current below 15 A or a learn time over 1.4 s.
s: Engine starts and stalls or will not start after a repair
Malfunction indicator lamp with reduced propulsion message
Electric drive unavailable
c: Offset learn not performed after replacing the inverter, motor or resolver
High voltage not reaching the inverter during the learn, e.g. contactor or HV cable fault
Loose three-phase ring terminals after a repair

P0C18.d: P0C18 is the motor B version of P0C17: the resolver offset of the second motor has not been learned and no valid earlier value is stored. GM performs the learn at key-off; it fails if motor speed exceeds 50 rpm, DC voltage stays below 192 V, phase current stays below 15 A or the learn takes longer than 1.4 s.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after a repair or module programming
Reduced propulsion or vehicle will not enter ready mode
Motor B unavailable for driving or charging
c: Offset learn not completed after replacing the inverter, motor B or its resolver
No high voltage at the drive motor control module, e.g. contactor fault or disconnected HV cable
Control module needs reprogramming to enable a wide position sensor learn

P0C19.d: P0C19 is a plausibility check: the torque that motor A actually delivers, calculated by the motor control processor, does not follow the slewed torque command. GM sets it when the difference exceeds 123 Nm for 0.1875 s within 0.2 s on the 2016 and 2018 tables, Type A, one trip; eAssist uses 36 Nm as Type B, two trips.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Electric drive shuts off and the engine takes over
Engine stop-start no longer works or a service hybrid system warning appears
c: Implausible rotor position signal from the motor A resolver or its wiring
Faulty phase current sensing distorting the calculated torque
Internal fault of the inverter power stage or motor winding

P0C1A.d: P0C1A compares the torque command for motor B with the torque the motor control processor calculates as actually delivered. GM's 2016, 2018 and 2019 tables set it when the difference exceeds 132 Nm for 0.1875 s in a 0.2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only while listed resolver and motor control faults are inactive.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp
Vehicle in limp mode with reduced propulsion
Hybrid system warning, engine runs more often
c: Short in the internal transmission wiring connector (Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid 21-008-23)
Implausible rotor position signal from the motor B resolver
Hybrid control or inverter module software requiring an update
Faulty phase current sensing for motor B

P0C1B.d: P0C1B is a protection code: the electronics that drive the auxiliary transmission fluid pump measure a valid but excessive internal temperature. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Engine auto-stop temporarily unavailable
Transmission or hybrid warning, MIL depending on manufacturer
Harsh engagement when driving off after a stop
c: High transmission fluid temperature from heavy load, towing or a weak fluid cooler
Pump running against high resistance (binding, clogged filter) and heating its driver
Poor heat transfer from the module (mounting, contamination) or internal module fault

P0C1C.d: P0C1C is the general circuit fault of the temperature sensor inside the auxiliary pump control module, used when the signal is invalid without fitting the low, high or range checks. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: Warning lamp or transmission message
Start-stop function inactive
c: Temperature sensor or its measuring circuit on the module board faulty
Unstable supply or ground of the pump module distorting the sensor reading
Moisture or fluid inside the module housing

P0C1D.d: P0C1D means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers an electrically valid value that does not fit the other temperatures in the vehicle. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL after repeated detection
Start-stop restricted or unavailable
c: Board temperature sensor drifted or measuring circuit out of tolerance
Reference value wrong because the transmission fluid or coolant temperature sensor is faulty
Internal fault of the pump control module

P0C1E.d: P0C1E reports that the signal voltage of the module's internal temperature sensor is below its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor, low voltage corresponds to a very high temperature, so a short to ground looks like an overheated board.
s: Pump switched off as if overheated, auto-stop unavailable
MIL after two drive cycles
c: Board temperature sensor or its signal path shorted to ground inside the module
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Fluid or moisture on the module board

P0C1F.d: P0C1F means the internal temperature sensor of the auxiliary pump module delivers a voltage above its valid range, which for an NTC thermistor reads as an implausibly cold board and usually indicates an open sensor path. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Start-stop restricted, pump in protective mode
c: Board temperature sensor open or its solder joint cracked
Measuring circuit of the pump control module faulty
Ground offset at the pump module shifting the sensor voltage

P0C20.d: P0C20 means at least one of the three motor phases of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump carries no current, typically an open lead, terminal or winding. GM uses it in the pump controller of the Chevrolet Volt (2011-15 tables) and the 2016 Cadillac ELR: with the inverter in Run, high voltage above 35 V and the rotor within 30 degrees of a phase axis, the peak current of that phase is checked; below 1 A for 200 cou
s: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon message
Reduced propulsion or no electric drive mode
Engine restart harsh or delayed
c: Motor connector of the pump not fully seated, or loose phase terminal
Open phase lead between pump inverter and motor
Power switch of one phase in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding in the pump motor

P0C21.d: P0C21 reports a low condition on the phase U, V or W circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, usually a phase lead shorted to ground or a voltage at a phase terminal that stays below what the inverter commands. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump off, no engine auto-stop
c: Phase lead chafed through and shorted to ground or the transmission case
Transmission fluid or water in the motor connector creating a leakage path
Low-side switch or phase sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Motor winding shorted to the stator core

P0C22.d: P0C22 reports a high condition on the U-V-W phase circuits of the auxiliary pump motor, for example a phase lead shorted to the supply or a phase voltage that stays high while the inverter should pull it down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL and hybrid or transmission warning
Pump shuts down, harsh engagement after stops
c: Phase lead shorted to supply voltage or to another phase
High-side switch of the pump inverter stuck conducting
Phase current sensing in the inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in the pump motor winding

P0C23.d: P0C23 is set by the controlling module, usually the PCM, TCM or hybrid controller, when the circuit to the auxiliary pump control module is open. J2012 does not name the line further; in practice it is the command or enable wire.
s: Start-stop no longer works
MIL or transmission warning
Harsh engagement after an engine stop
c: Open command or enable wire between controller and pump module
Pushed-out or corroded terminal at the pump module or controller connector
Input stage of the pump control module faulty

P0C24.d: P0C24 means the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module is held low, typically a short to ground on the command line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: No engine auto-stop
MIL or transmission warning
c: Command wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed at the transmission case
Fluid or corrosion in the pump connector pulling the line low
Output stage in the PCM/TCM or input of the pump module faulty

P0C25.d: P0C25 reports that the circuit from the controlling module to the auxiliary pump control module sits high, for instance a command wire shorted to battery voltage or an output that cannot pull the line down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL or transmission warning
Pump runs continuously or start-stop is disabled
c: Command wire shorted to battery or another supply voltage
Output stage in the PCM/TCM stuck high
Input stage of the pump control module faulty

P0C26.d: P0C26 is the general motor current fault of auxiliary pump A: the current drawn does not match what the commanded operating point should need, without clearly being too low or too high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL or transmission warning
Harsh engagement after an auto-stop
Start-stop deactivated
c: Low or aerated transmission fluid at the pump intake
Pump binding or contaminated, changing the motor load
Current sensing in the pump driver implausible
Outdated control software of the pump or controlling module

P0C27.d: P0C27 means motor A of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump draws less current than expected, a sign that the pump is not loaded, for example because it sucks air or turns without delivering. Ford documents it twice.
s: MIL on
Harsh transmission engagement after a start-stop event
c: Air entering the pump supply tube (Ford 6F35, new tube with check ball)
Calibration of PCM and hybrid module (Ford Fusion/C-Max Energi)
Low transmission fluid level letting the pump draw air
High resistance or open circuit in the pump motor wiring

P0C28.d: P0C28 is the overcurrent protection of auxiliary pump motor A. GM uses it on Volt, ELR and later hybrids: the inverter trips when any of the U, V or W phases exceeds 35 A, in 2016 within about 4 ms of a 62 ms window, or when the d-axis current falls below a stator temperature limit, Type A, MIL on the first trip.
s: MIL or service wrench lamp
Auxiliary pump shuts down, no auto-stop or electric mode
c: Pump control software faulty (Cadillac CT6 update 18199, Ford Energi TSB 18-2282)
Pump seized, contaminated or running against blocked flow
Short between motor phases or to ground
Current sensing or power stage in the pump inverter faulty

P0C29.d: P0C29 means the driver stage of auxiliary pump A does not behave as commanded, for instance the pump does not reach its target or the activation is reported as implausible. Volkswagen Group documents it on the 7-speed DSG 0GC (DQ381): VW lists P0C29 for the 2018 Golf R as implausible activation of auxiliary hydraulic pump 1 (V475), often with clutch and gear actuator codes as consequences; Audi's bulletin for the 201
s: Gearbox Malfunction warning in the instrument cluster
Consequential clutch or gear actuator codes, limp mode
c: Auxiliary hydraulic pump V475 of early production faulty (VW/Audi 0GC)
Poor contact at the pump electrical connection
Transmission control software not updated per service action

P0C2A.d: P0C2A means motor A of the auxiliary pump is commanded but does not turn, or turns far slower than required. Ford documents it in TSB 17-2056 for the 2016 F-150 2.7L with start-stop built from 1 May 2016: with the fluid above 38 °C the technician commands the pump through the PCM at duty cycles from 20 to 90 percent; if it runs, the PCM gets new software, if not, the auxiliary pump is replaced.
s: MIL on
Start-stop inactive, harsh engagement after stops
c: Auxiliary pump seized or jammed by debris (Ford F-150 2.7L replaces the pump)
PCM calibration causing false stall detection (Ford TSB 17-2056)
Very cold, thick fluid or wrong fluid type raising drag
Open phase so the motor cannot develop torque

P0C2B.d: P0C2B concerns the status signal the auxiliary pump control module sends back to the controlling module. GM uses it on the Two-Mode hybrid trucks and SUVs (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra, 2ML70): the hybrid controller expects a complete fault status message from the pump controller every 1.5 s; if it is missing or incomplete for 9.75 s with the vehicle in Run or Crank, the code sets as Type B, MIL after tw
s: MIL after two drive cycles
Bumps, lulls or surges around auto-stops
c: Wiring or terminal tension fault between hybrid controller and pump control module
Early pump control module (GM date code 089-11 or older)
Key held in crank for a long time during a no-start

P0C2C.d: P0C2C means the feedback signal from the auxiliary pump control module is present and electrically valid but does not make sense, for example a reported speed or status that contradicts the command. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Service Vehicle Soon or MIL
Reduced propulsion power or no start-stop
c: Electronics of the pump module reporting wrong status or speed
Intermittent contact on the feedback line distorting the signal
Pump not following the command mechanically, so feedback and command differ

P0C2D.d: P0C2D reports that the feedback signal from the electric transmission fluid pump module stays low, below its valid range. GM documents it for the 2021-23 Chevrolet Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV in bulletin 21-NA-148: the driver sees Propulsion Power is Reduced and a Service Vehicle Soon lamp, with P0C2D, P2797 or P2798 stored.
s: Propulsion Power is Reduced message
Service Vehicle Soon lamp
c: Faulty solder joints in the electric transmission fluid pump (Chevrolet Bolt, GM 21-NA-148)

P0C2E.d: P0C2E means the feedback line from the auxiliary pump control module sits above its valid range, for example shorted to supply voltage or no longer pulled down by the module. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: MIL or Service Vehicle Soon lamp
Start-stop or electric drive restricted
c: Feedback line shorted to supply voltage
Output stage of the pump control module no longer switching
Lost ground at the pump module letting the line float high

P0C2F.d: P0C2F is an internal plausibility check of the hybrid control processor: the engine speed it reads through its own sensor path must match other speed information. In GM's Two-Mode truck tables (12OBDG06, 13OBDG06) the HCP compares its SPI-sensed engine speed with the calculated transmission input speed and with the engine speed received over CAN; a deviation beyond 250 rpm above 1500 rpm, with a wider band at lower s
s: MIL or hybrid system warning
One pedal drive or regenerative functions switched off (Ford Mach-E)
Reduced hybrid assist or limited power
c: Control module software flagging the comparison falsely (Ford Mach-E, fixed by reprogramming)
Speed signals disagree because of a faulty input or a disturbed CAN signal
Internal fault of the hybrid control module

P0C30.d: P0C30 is the counterpart of P0A7D: the battery controller finds that the state of charge of the high-voltage pack stays above its usable window. CARB requires hybrid OBD to flag a state of charge that can no longer be kept inside the manufacturer's range.
s: MIL after two trips
Reduced or no regenerative braking
Changed brake pedal feel and higher fuel consumption
c: Wrong SOC estimate from a drifting pack current or voltage measurement
Battery or hybrid control software not drawing the charge down as intended
Electric assist blocked by another fault, so the pack cannot discharge

P0C31.d: P0C31 reports that the cooling circuit of a second power inverter does not remove heat as expected; inverter A has its own code, P0A93. Vehicles with two separately cooled power electronics units, for example a front and a rear drive unit, need this second code.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Reduced drive power, especially under load or in heat
Coolant level low in the electronics reservoir
c: Low coolant level or air trapped in the inverter B circuit
Weak or failed electric coolant pump of the circuit
Clogged radiator or inoperative cooling fan

P0C32.d: P0C32 is the functional check of the battery thermal system that CARB asks for. GM tunes it per vehicle: the 2012 Volt (12OBDG01A) fails it when the average pack temperature stays above 40 °C in active cooling or below −17 °C in active heating, after 4200 s or 9000 s, Type A, one trip.
s: MIL and hybrid system warning
Reduced electric range or assist
Charging system or battery warning message (eAssist)
c: Battery cooling fan stopping at low 12 V system voltage (GM eAssist)
Low coolant, air or a weak pump in a liquid-cooled pack circuit
Blocked cooling air intake or ducts of an air-cooled pack
Failed pack heater or chiller valve

P0C33.d: Battery temperature sensor F is the sixth thermistor in the high-voltage pack; GM's Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the F codes under temperature sensor 6 of nine. P0C33 is the general circuit code for an electrical fault the controller does not classify as low, high or erratic.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Reduced power or charging rate
Battery cooling running more than usual
c: Loose or corroded connector of sensor F at the sensing board
Faulty input on the battery sensing board or module

P0C34.d: P0C34 checks whether sensor F, GM's sensor 6, agrees with the rest of the pack. The controller compares its reading with the average of the other battery temperature sensors.
s: MIL on after two trips
Battery too cold or reduced power message
Limited charge and discharge power
c: Sensor F drifting or poorly seated on its cell group
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)
Real local temperature difference from a weak cell group or uneven cooling

P0C35.d: Sensor F is an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so its voltage drops as temperature rises; a short to ground looks like an extremely hot cell group. Low refers to the signal, not to the temperature.
s: MIL after two trips
Battery cooling running at high speed
Strongly reduced charge and drive power
c: Sensor F signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Faulty input on the battery sensing board

P0C36.d: P0C36 means the voltage from battery temperature sensor F sits above its valid range. With GM's NTC thermistor and pull-up, an open circuit, a broken wire or an unplugged connector pulls the input up and reads as an impossibly cold cell group.
s: MIL after two trips
Battery too cold, plug in to warm message
Reduced electric power
c: Open circuit or unlatched connector of sensor F
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)

P0C37.d: P0C37 targets a sensor F signal that jumps instead of following the slow temperature change of a heavy battery. GM documents the logic in its 2016 to 2018 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 17OBDG02, 18OBDG02): every 100 ms the controller adds up the absolute changes of the sensor value over a window of 10 samples; a sum above 10 fails the window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 set the code as Type B, two trips, with system vol
s: MIL after two trips
Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads
Temporarily reduced power
c: Loose terminal or connector of sensor F not fully latched after pack work
Cracked sensor wire with intermittent contact
Faulty battery sensing board, often with several sensors affected

P0C38.d: The DC/DC converter steps the high-voltage battery down to the 12 V system and replaces the alternator in hybrids and EVs. Its power stage carries temperature sensors so the controller can derate before the semiconductors overheat.
s: Hybrid system warning light
12 V charging reduced or switched off
Code appearing after the car has stood for a long time
c: Control unit software misjudging the sensor after long parking (Hyundai Palisade Hybrid)
Fault in the circuit of sensor A inside the converter or power control unit
Internal fault of the DC/DC converter requiring replacement

P0C39.d: P0C39 is the plausibility check of DC/DC converter temperature sensor A: its reading lies within the electrical range but does not fit the converter's operating state or a second sensor. FCA uses it on the 2021 Ram 1500 with the 3.6 litre eTorque mild hybrid, where the code is called temperature sensor 1 performance.
s: MIL, after one trip with updated Ram software
Mild hybrid assist or 12 V supply reduced
c: Outdated hybrid control software (Ram 1500 eTorque, bulletin 08-037-21)
Sensor A drifting or with poor thermal contact to the power stage
Uneven cooling of the converter making the readings disagree

P0C3A.d: P0C3A means the signal of DC/DC converter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. Low refers to the signal voltage: with an NTC thermistor and pull-up, as GM uses for its hybrid temperature sensors, a short to ground or a failed element reads as extreme heat.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning
12 V battery warning, system voltage dropping
Reduced power or restricted functions
c: Sensor A signal shorted to ground inside the converter or its harness
Shorted temperature element A, usually requiring converter replacement
Converter really overheated due to a cooling fault

P0C3B.d: P0C3B reports a signal from DC/DC converter temperature sensor A above its valid range, typically a short to positive or an open circuit pulled up by the input. Mercedes-Benz documents it on series 243 (EQB) and 465 (G-Class, including the electric G 580): information LI54.10-P-079533 describes P0C3B00 as a short circuit to positive of temperature sensor A, stored together with P0E9700, P0E5400 and P0C4000 after faul
s: Red 12 V battery warning in the cluster
White or yellow high-voltage system warning
12 V battery no longer charged while driving
c: Faulty wake-up behaviour of the converter putting it into an error state (Mercedes 243/465)
Open circuit or short to positive in the sensor A circuit
Internal defect of the DC/DC converter

P0C3C.d: P0C3C covers a signal from DC/DC converter temperature sensor A that drops out or jumps for short moments while staying mostly within range. The heat sink of a converter warms and cools slowly, so fast jumps point to the signal path rather than to real temperature changes.
s: Intermittent hybrid or EV warning
Occasional 12 V charging interruptions
c: Loose terminal or moisture at the converter connector
Harness damaged by vibration with intermittent contact

P0C3D.d: P0C3D is the general circuit code for the second temperature sensor of the DC/DC converter, which turns high-voltage battery power into 12 V supply. Converters with two sensors watch separate parts of the power stage or cross-check one sensor against the other.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning
12 V battery warning
c: Connector or wiring fault in the sensor B circuit
Failed temperature element B inside the converter
Converter or hybrid control software misjudging the sensor

P0C3E.d: P0C3E flags DC/DC converter temperature sensor B as electrically valid but implausible, for instance when it disagrees with sensor A or with what the converter load should produce. FCA uses it on the 2021 Ram 1500 with the 3.6 litre eTorque mild hybrid under the name temperature sensor 2 performance.
s: MIL, after one trip with updated Ram software
Mild hybrid assist or 12 V supply reduced
c: Outdated hybrid control software (Ram 1500 eTorque, bulletin 08-037-21)
Sensor B drifting or with poor thermal contact
Uneven converter cooling making sensors A and B disagree

P0C3F.d: P0C3F is stored when the voltage from the second temperature sensor of the DC/DC converter falls below the lowest plausible value. These sensors are normally NTC thermistors fed through a pull-up resistor, so a low voltage corresponds to an extremely hot reading; a short to ground or a shorted element produces exactly that.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning in the cluster
12 V battery warning or falling on-board voltage
Reduced power or switched-off comfort consumers
c: Sensor B signal line shorted to ground in the converter or harness
Shorted thermistor B, usually only fixable by replacing the converter
Converter actually overheating because its cooling fails

P0C40.d: P0C40 means the second temperature sensor of the DC/DC converter delivers a voltage above its valid window, which on a thermistor circuit points to a short to positive or an open line pulled up to the reference. Mercedes-Benz documents it for the EQB (series 243) and the G-Class including the electric G 580 (series 465).
s: Red 12 V battery message in the instrument cluster
White or yellow high-voltage warning
12 V battery no longer charged while driving
c: Converter entering a fault state after incorrect wake-up (Mercedes 243/465)
Open circuit or short to positive in the sensor B wiring
Internal defect of the DC/DC converter

P0C41.d: P0C41 concerns a reading from DC/DC converter temperature sensor B that jumps or briefly drops out while it mostly remains inside the valid range. A converter heat sink changes temperature slowly, so abrupt steps indicate a signal problem rather than real heating.
s: Hybrid or EV warning that comes and goes
Short interruptions of 12 V charging
c: Loose terminal or moisture at the converter connector
Harness chafed or cracked by vibration

P0C42.d: P0C42 is the general circuit code for the first coolant temperature sensor in the liquid loop of a hybrid or EV battery, typically placed at the pack inlet. The battery controller uses it to decide when to pump, heat or chill the coolant.
s: Check engine lamp, often without other complaints
Battery cooling or heating running on substitute values
Reduced charging or drive power in hot or cold weather
c: Battery controller software flagging the circuit wrongly (Volvo XC90 T8)
Corroded or loose connector or damaged wire at the coolant sensor

P0C43.d: P0C43 flags battery coolant temperature sensor A as electrically valid but not believable. GM's 2019 hybrid tables describe a cold-soak comparison: once all high-voltage contactors and the battery heater have been off for at least 14,400 s, the hybrid controller compares inlet coolant temperature with the average cell temperature and with outside air, failing when the gaps reach about 23 °C and 22 °C; 8 s out of 10 s
s: MIL after a cold start, often with no other complaint
Battery thermal management working on substitute values
c: Too tight plausibility limits in the control software (Audi Q5 TFSI e, update 80C9)
Coolant sensor A drifting away from its characteristic
Added resistance in the sensor circuit shifting the reading

P0C44.d: P0C44 reports that the voltage of battery coolant temperature sensor A is too low. The sensor is an NTC thermistor, so a low voltage translates into a very hot reading, and a short to ground or a shorted element is the classic cause.
s: MIL and hybrid or EV system message
Coolant temperature shown implausibly high in live data
Limited charging or drive power
c: Sensor signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Coolant or water in the connector bridging the pins

P0C45.d: P0C45 indicates that the signal of battery coolant temperature sensor A sits near the reference voltage. On an NTC circuit with pull-up this looks like extreme cold and usually comes from an open circuit, an unplugged connector or a short to voltage.
s: MIL after two trips
Coolant temperature shown at about -40 °C in live data
Reduced charging power in extreme temperatures
c: Open signal or ground wire, or connector not latched
Signal wire shorted to a voltage source

P0C46.d: P0C46 points to a battery coolant temperature signal that jumps faster than liquid in the loop can physically change temperature. GM's 2019 hybrid tables explain the check: every 100 ms the hybrid controller takes the difference to the previous inlet coolant value, adds up ten of these absolute steps and counts a failure when the sum exceeds 64 °C.
s: MIL that may go out again for a while
Jumping coolant temperature in live data
c: Loose or spread terminal at the coolant sensor connector
Corrosion at connector or ground point
Harness rubbing or cracked near the battery coolant lines

P0C47.d: P0C47 means the controller sees an electrical fault on the line that commands battery coolant pump A. GM's 2019 tables catch open, short to ground and short to power by current: with the pump on, less than 200 mA or more than 3 A on the control line count as failures, with the pump off less than 120 µA; 4 s within 5 s set a Type B code.
s: MIL, frequently the only sign
Electrical or drive system warning with reduced power
Vehicle refuses to become ready to drive
c: Corroded or painted ground point or corroded pump connector (Porsche Cayenne 92A)
Corroded splice or chafed harness in the pump circuit (Audi Q4 e-tron, Bentley)
Failed electric coolant pump or its relay

P0C48.d: P0C48 narrows a fault on the control line of battery coolant pump A down to a signal that stays too low, as caused by a short to ground or a driver output that cannot pull the line up. Ford lists the code for the 2020 Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Lincoln Aviator with the hybrid powertrain.
s: MIL on
Hybrid system message, battery power possibly limited
c: Battery control module software (Ford/Lincoln 2020 hybrids, TSB 20-2345)
Pump control wire shorted to ground
Internal fault in the pump electronics pulling the line low

P0C49.d: P0C49 is set when the control signal to battery coolant pump A remains too high, for example because the line is shorted to battery voltage or, on a pulled-up input, interrupted. Ford uses it on the 2020 Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Lincoln Aviator hybrids.
s: MIL on
Battery power reduced during long climbs or fast charging
c: Battery control module software (Ford/Lincoln 2020 hybrids, TSB 20-2293/20-2345)
Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Control line interrupted at the pump connector

P0C4A.d: P0C4A says pump A runs electrically but does not achieve its cooling effect. The 2011 Chevrolet Volt fails the test when the pump has been on for over 60 s and the pack inlet coolant temperature has moved by less than 5 °C, rated Type B.
s: MIL shortly after cooling system work
Electric drive warning, reduced power or capped EV speed
Gurgling noise from the coolant loop
c: Air trapped in the battery coolant loop, often after a coolant service
Low coolant level or a leak in the low-temperature loop

P0C4B.d: P0C4B refers to the power feed of battery coolant pump A rather than its command line: the controller sees no or only an implausible supply voltage at the pump, typically because a fuse, relay, connector or wire in the feed is open. Ford documents the code on its 2020 hybrids.
s: MIL on
Battery coolant pump not running, power limited when warm
c: Battery control module software (Ford Escape HEV, Explorer and Aviator 2020)
Blown fuse or failed relay in the pump supply
Open feed wire or pushed-out pin at the pump connector

P0C4C.d: P0C4C reports that the supply voltage reaching battery coolant pump A is below the expected level while the circuit is not fully open. Typical reasons are high resistance in the feed, a corroded fuse contact, a weak relay, a poor ground or a short to ground that drags the line down.
s: MIL or hybrid or EV warning
Coolant pump running slowly or intermittently
Battery power reduced when the pack warms up
c: High resistance from corroded fuse, relay contacts or connector
Supply wire chafed and shorted to ground

P0C4D.d: P0C4D is the counterpart to P0C4C: the voltage measured on the supply of battery coolant pump A is higher than the controller allows. That can come from a feed wire shorted to another, more highly loaded circuit, from a relay that stays closed when the pump should be off, or from an overall excessive on-board voltage, for example a faulty DC/DC converter.
s: MIL or hybrid or EV warning
Coolant pump running although the system is switched off
c: Supply wire shorted to another voltage-carrying circuit
Excessive 12 V system voltage from a faulty DC/DC converter

P0C4E.d: P0C4E says the resolver offset of drive motor A was learned, yet the learned value is unacceptable. That offset lines up the zero point of the resolver with the rotor magnets.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp, often first noticed after a repair
Jerk or rough feel when switching between electric and hybrid drive
Reduced electric drive power
c: Resolver or rotor position shifted after replacing the motor, resolver stator or transaxle
Internal transaxle fault on affected Kia Sorento PHEV models (TSB TRA112)
Hybrid or motor control software that needs an update
Damaged resolver that delivers a shifted angle

P0C4F.d: P0C4F covers the second traction motor: its resolver offset learn finished, but the angle it produced lies outside what the controller will accept. GM applies the same two tests as for motor A, an absolute correction above 30 degrees or a change of over 10 degrees against the value kept from earlier learns, both checked at key-off with the rotor nearly still and more than 192 V available.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp after shutdown cycles
Reduced propulsion or motor B unavailable
Unusual noise or shudder under electric drive
c: Motor B resolver stator fitted in a different position after a repair
Learn disturbed by a moving rotor or unstable high voltage at key-off
Damaged motor B resolver giving a shifted angle

P0C50.d: A resolver has two pickup windings set 90 degrees apart, one giving a sine and one a cosine signal. The codes P0C50 onward judge each of those circuits on its own, while P0A3F to P0A43 judge the combined angle signal.
s: Hybrid or drive system warning together with the check engine lamp
Electric drive switched off or reduced power
Vehicle may not reach ready mode
c: Open wire or loose terminal in the Circuit A (first pickup winding) lines
Corroded or damaged connector between resolver and motor control module
Defective pickup winding inside the resolver stator
Fault in the resolver input stage of the motor control module

P0C51.d: P0C51 means the first resolver winding of motor A (Circuit A) delivers a signal that is electrically present but not believable, for example unsteady or out of step with the second winding. Bentley uses it on 2025 Continental GT, GTC and Flying Spur hybrids, logged by the e-drive control unit at address 0051 next to P0A4000 and later P0C5B00, with a drive system message in the cluster.
s: Drive system fault message in the instrument cluster
No electric or hybrid driving mode available
Fault may come and go with temperature or vibration
c: Weak terminal grip or bent pins at the sensor or power electronics connector
Moisture, oil or corrosion in the resolver connectors
Faulty 90-degree connector on the affected Bentley models (TPI 2080242/3)

P0C52.d: P0C52 reports that the DC reference level on Circuit A of the motor A resolver, the S1/S3 winding in GM terms, has dropped too low, which points to a short to ground or a line pulled down. GM fails it below 0.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2012 two-mode trucks, 2013 eAssist and 2016 ELR, and below 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt.
s: Check engine lamp, often with P0C5C stored at the same time
Electric drive shut off or power reduced
On some hybrids the engine runs constantly or the car will not start
c: Chafed or pinched transmission harness shorting a Circuit A line to ground (Bentley TPI 2066714)
Water or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted S1/S3 winding inside the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input in the motor control module

P0C53.d: P0C53 is the high counterpart of P0C52: the reference level on the S1/S3 winding circuit of the motor A resolver rises above its window, typical of a short to a voltage source or an open line that floats up. GM uses an upper limit of 4.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2013 eAssist and 2016 Volt and ELR, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and only 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Sierra and Silverado hybrids.
s: Check engine lamp with hybrid system message
Reduced propulsion or electric drive unavailable
Rough engine running on vehicles that use motor A for starting
c: Open S1 or S3 line or a terminal that has backed out, letting the input drift high
Circuit A line shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the harness
Broken S1/S3 winding in the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input in the motor control module

P0C54.d: P0C54 stands for short dropouts or jumps on Circuit A of the motor A resolver that never last long enough to count as a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning lamp that appears and disappears between trips
Brief loss of electric drive or a short jerk
Fault often gone after a restart
c: Loose or poorly crimped terminal in a Circuit A line
Harness rubbing or flexing at a point that moves with the powertrain
Moisture or contamination in the resolver plug

P0C55.d: P0C55 is the general circuit code for the first pickup winding (Circuit A) of the resolver on the second traction motor. It applies when the motor B controller recognises a fault on that winding but cannot assign it to a low or high level.
s: Check engine lamp with hybrid system warning
Motor B unavailable, reduced propulsion
Engine may run more often because the second motor is offline
c: Open wire or loose terminal in the motor B Circuit A lines
Damaged or corroded motor B resolver connector
Defective first pickup winding in the motor B resolver

P0C56.d: P0C56 flags a plausibility problem on Circuit A of the motor B resolver: the winding is connected and its level sits inside the electrical window, yet the signal it carries does not fit, for instance because it wanders or no longer matches the second winding. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Hybrid warning and check engine lamp
Motor B torque limited or switched off
Occasional shudder when motor B takes load
c: Poor pin fit or contamination at the motor B resolver connector
Damaged shield or twisted pair letting interference onto Circuit A
Motor B resolver winding with weakened output

P0C57.d: P0C57 means the reference level on Circuit A of the motor B resolver, the S1/S3 winding in GM wiring, has sunk below its limit. GM checks it exactly like the motor A line: under 0.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks, under 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt, with Type A on the early cars and Type B from 2016.
s: Service engine soon lamp, current or in history
Often stored together with P0C58 and P0C62
Reduced propulsion
c: Faulty motor B position sensor (resolver stator) on Volt and ELR (GM PIC5856)
Circuit A line of motor B shorted to ground in the harness
Drive motor generator control module not on the latest calibration

P0C58.d: P0C58 sets when the S1/S3 winding circuit of the motor B resolver shows a reference level above its window, as from an open lead drifting up or a short to voltage. GM limits are 4.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode trucks, with the fast high-side timing of 20 out of 30 samples on early cars.
s: Check engine lamp, frequently together with P0C62
Reduced propulsion power
Fault may only be in history memory
c: Faulty motor B position sensor on 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR (GM PIC5856)
Open S1 or S3 line or spread terminal at the resolver connector
Motor control module running an older calibration

P0C59.d: P0C59 reports that Circuit A of the motor B resolver drops out or jumps for moments only, without a fault that persists as low, high or implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short loss of motor B assistance or a jerk
Intermittent start problems on some hybrids
c: Poorly crimped or loose terminal in the motor B Circuit A path
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes
Water ingress at the resolver or pass-through connector

P0C5A.d: P0C5A is the base circuit code for Circuit B, the second pickup winding of the motor A resolver; GM calls it the S2/S4 winding, set 90 degrees from the S1/S3 winding of Circuit A. The code is meant for a fault on that winding which the controller cannot class as a low or high level.
s: Check engine lamp with drive system warning
Electric drive limited or unavailable
Vehicle may refuse to enter ready mode
c: Open wire or loose terminal in the S2/S4 (Circuit B) lines
Defective second pickup winding in the resolver stator

P0C5B.d: P0C5B is set when the second resolver winding of motor A (Circuit B) stays within its electrical limits yet carries a signal that does not make sense next to the first winding. Bentley added it in revision 3 of bulletin 2080242 for the Continental GT, GTC and Flying Spur hybrids: P0C5B00 now appears alongside P0C5100 and P0A4000, which shows that both windings lose plausibility at once when the shared connection is p
s: Drive system fault shown in the cluster
Electric drive mode not available
Usually stored together with P0C51 and P0A40
c: Insufficient terminal grip at the sensor or power electronics connector
Faulty 90-degree connector on affected Bentley hybrids (TPI 2080242/3)
Corrosion, oil or moisture in the resolver plugs

P0C5C.d: P0C5C tells that the reference level on the S2/S4 winding of the motor A resolver, Circuit B, has fallen below its floor. GM uses 0.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2012 two-mode trucks, 2013 eAssist and the 2016 Volt and ELR, 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt; the low side needs a longer confirmation than the high side, for example 0.525 s within 0.8375 s on the 2016 Volt.
s: Engine warning light, often with P0C52 and a motor temperature code
Electric drive limited or switched off
On mild hybrids loss of start-stop and assist
c: Transmission harness chafed or pinched, grounding an S2/S4 line (Bentley TPI 2066714)
Moisture or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted S2/S4 winding in the resolver stator

P0C5D.d: P0C5D means the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor A resolver, Circuit B, reads a reference level above its ceiling. This hints at an open wire whose input floats toward the supply, or contact with a voltage-carrying conductor.
s: Check engine lamp after one or two trips depending on the vehicle
Electric assist or drive unavailable
Auto stop disabled on mild hybrids
c: Open S2 or S4 wire or backed-out terminal
S2/S4 line touching a voltage-carrying conductor
Broken S2/S4 winding in the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

P0C5E.d: P0C5E captures brief interruptions or spikes on Circuit B, the second winding of the motor A resolver, that clear again before a firm low, high or plausibility fault can be confirmed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning light appearing only now and then
Momentary drop of electric torque
No fault found on a stationary check
c: Loose or weak terminal in the S2/S4 path
Harness rubbing on the transmission because of a missing or broken clip

P0C5F.d: P0C5F is the umbrella circuit code for Circuit B of the motor B resolver, which GM wires as the S2/S4 winding of the second traction motor. It fits a fault on that winding that the controller notices but cannot assign to a low or high reading.
s: Hybrid warning and check engine lamp
Motor B shut off, lower propulsion
Possible no-start on hybrids that crank with motor B
c: Open wire or loose terminal in the motor B S2/S4 lines
Damaged motor B resolver or pass-through connector
Defective second pickup winding in the motor B resolver

P0C60.d: P0C60 indicates that the second winding of the motor B resolver (Circuit B) is electrically intact but delivers values the controller rejects as unrealistic, for example an amplitude that no longer agrees with the first winding or an angle that jumps against the measured speed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Hybrid system warning with check engine lamp
Motor B output limited
Vibration or noise when motor B is under load
c: Raised contact resistance at the motor B resolver connector
Motor B resolver stator shifted or damaged
Interference from the high-voltage phase cables through a damaged shield

P0C61.d: P0C61 reports a reference level below the lower limit on the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor B resolver. GM uses 0.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks, 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt, and needs the low reading for 50 of 80 samples on early cars, 0.25 s within 0.375 s on the 2019 model.
s: Engine does not crank or cranks only intermittently
Check engine lamp with several resolver codes of motor B
Reduced propulsion
c: Poor crimp at the transmission pass-through connector (GM PIP4607A, 2008 Tahoe/Yukon Hybrid)
S2/S4 line of motor B shorted to ground
Shorted S2/S4 winding in the motor B resolver

P0C62.d: P0C62 means the reference level on the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor B resolver climbs above its upper limit. GM triggers it at 4.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and ELR, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode trucks; on the 2016 Volt the level must stay high for 0.2125 s within 0.3125 s, rated Type B over two trips.
s: Service engine soon lamp, often with P0C58
Reduced propulsion power
Code may return after clearing until the sensor is replaced
c: Faulty motor B position sensor on 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR (GM PIC5856)
Open S2 or S4 wire or terminal backed out of the connector
Drive motor generator control module without the latest calibration

P0C63.d: P0C63 is reserved for short-lived dropouts or erratic jumps on Circuit B, the second winding of the motor B resolver, that do not settle into a steady fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Occasional start problems or short loss of motor B
Fault not present during a workshop check
c: Weak crimp or loose terminal in the motor B S2/S4 path, including pass-through connectors
Intermittent wire break near moving powertrain parts
Moisture or corrosion causing unstable contact

P0C64.d: P0C64 is the catch-all entry for the first pickup circuit of the generator resolver, the sensor that reports rotor angle so the inverter can energise the generator phases at the right moment. It is used when the controller judges that circuit faulty without sorting the fault into low, high, implausible or sporadic.
s: Hybrid system or malfunction indicator lamp on
Engine runs but the high-voltage battery is no longer charged by the generator
Reduced power or hybrid functions disabled
c: Open, chafed or shorted lead in the first resolver pickup winding circuit
Corroded or loose resolver connector between generator and inverter
Damaged pickup winding inside the generator resolver stator
Fault in the generator control electronics of the inverter or power drive unit

P0C65.d: P0C65 flags circuit A of the generator resolver as electrically present but not believable. The trace stays between the hard low and high limits, yet its amplitude, centre voltage or relation to the second winding no longer fits the rotor angle the controller expects, for example after the sensor stator has shifted or when the phase cables couple noise into it.
s: Hybrid system warning light
Generator use restricted, less charging while driving
Occasional roughness when the engine starts or stops in hybrid mode
c: Resolver stator loose or shifted, for instance after work on the generator or transaxle
Interference from the phase cables because of a misrouted or damaged resolver harness
Partially damaged winding that weakens the circuit A signal
Generator control software that misjudges a sound signal

P0C66.d: P0C66 means the signal of circuit A of the generator resolver has dropped below its lower limit. Mitsubishi uses it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV for the sine winding: the generator control unit, supplied with at least 8 V, watches the line continuously and sets the code when the sine voltage stays at or below 2.000 V for 0.21 s.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning shortly after switching on
Generator out of service, no charging by the engine
Reduced driving power
c: Sine lead of the resolver shorted to ground or to the housing
Shorted or damaged sine winding in the generator resolver
Faulty input stage in the power drive unit (generator control unit)
Damaged or contaminated resolver connector pins

P0C67.d: With P0C67 the controller sees circuit A of the generator resolver stuck above its upper limit. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV Mitsubishi assigns it to the sine winding and trips it once that voltage stays at or above 4.900 V for 0.21 s; the check runs continuously while the generator control unit has 8 V or more.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Engine-driven charging stops, battery charge falls faster
Power limitation or hybrid functions switched off
c: Sine lead of the resolver shorted to a supply or excitation potential
Open sine lead that floats high at the input stage
Faulty resolver input in the power drive unit
Insulation fault between windings inside the resolver

P0C68.d: P0C68 is stored when circuit A of the generator resolver drops out or jumps for short moments and then looks normal again, so neither the low nor the high limit is held long enough to set P0C66 or P0C67. Vibration at a connector, a chafed lead or contacts that loosen with heat are the usual suspects.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief jolts or interruptions in generator operation
Fault appears mainly on bad roads or after long drives
c: Resolver connector with poor contact that opens under vibration
Harness rubbing through intermittently in the transaxle or generator area
Bursts of interference from nearby phase cables due to harness routing
Contact or winding joint that fails only at high temperature

P0C69.d: P0C69 is the general fault entry for the second pickup winding of the generator resolver. A resolver needs both windings, set 90 degrees apart, to give an unambiguous rotor angle; with only one, the inverter can no longer place the current in the generator phases correctly.
s: Hybrid warning or malfunction indicator lamp
Generator switched off, battery is no longer recharged by the engine
Limited driving power
c: Open or damaged lead in the second resolver pickup winding circuit
Bent, corroded or pushed-back pins at the resolver connector
Faulty second pickup winding in the resolver stator
Internal fault in the generator control electronics

P0C6A.d: P0C6A concerns circuit B of the generator resolver, the cosine side at Mitsubishi: its signal stays inside the electrical limits but does not agree with what the controller expects. Because sine and cosine together describe one angle, a cosine trace with the wrong amplitude or a drifting centre shows up as a mismatch against circuit A, even though no line is shorted.
s: Hybrid warning lamp
Generator used only partly or not at all
Unusual noise or vibration from the transaxle under load
c: Loose or twisted resolver stator changing the cosine amplitude
Partially shorted cosine winding with weakened output
Noise from phase leads due to damaged shielding or poor routing
High contact resistance in the circuit B connector

P0C6B.d: P0C6B tells you that circuit B of the generator resolver, the cosine winding, reads too low. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi stores it if the cosine signal is no higher than 2.000 V throughout 0.21 s; the test never pauses while the generator control unit receives 8 V or more.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp right after switching on
No charging of the drive battery by the engine
Reduced performance in hybrid mode
c: Cosine lead of the resolver shorted to ground
Pinched or crushed resolver harness near the transaxle
Shorted cosine winding in the generator resolver
Faulty cosine input in the power drive unit

P0C6C.d: P0C6C is the high-side fault of circuit B in the generator resolver. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV, where circuit B is the cosine winding, Mitsubishi triggers it when the cosine voltage sits at 4.900 V or above for 0.21 s; the monitor stays active as long as the generator control unit is supplied with 8 V.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Generator inactive, state of charge drops while driving
Engine may run more often or the car limits power
c: Cosine lead shorted to a supply or excitation line
Damaged resolver connector with bridged pins
Internal fault in the power drive unit holding the generator control unit
Open cosine lead that drifts high at the input

P0C6D.d: P0C6D records short, irregular disturbances on circuit B of the generator resolver: the signal flickers, loses samples or jumps, but each event is too brief to count as a hard low or high reading (P0C6B, P0C6C). Because the angle is computed from both windings, even short glitches on the second winding can make the inverter lose track of the rotor for a moment, which may be felt as a jolt or a brief break in charging
s: Intermittent warning lamp
Short jerks or charging interruptions in hybrid mode
Fault hard to reproduce in the workshop
c: Terminal with reduced contact pressure in the circuit B connector
Moisture entering through a damaged connector seal
Harness moving against a bracket or edge and breaking contact
Interference spikes from phase cables near the resolver lines

P0C6E.d: P0C6E compares two battery temperature sensors, A and B, with each other rather than judging either one alone. After a long rest the pack should be close to one temperature, so a lasting gap between the two points to a sensor that reads wrongly while staying electrically valid.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Reduced charge and discharge power
Battery fan or cooling running more than usual
c: Thermistor A or B drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor no longer seated against its cell or module
Genuine temperature difference from uneven cooling or a weak cell group
Battery management software with an over-sensitive comparison

P0C6F.d: P0C6F sets when battery temperature sensors B and C disagree by more than the calibrated margin. Sensor B also takes part in the A/B check (P0C6E), so the pattern of stored codes helps: if P0C6E and P0C6F appear together, B is the shared suspect, while P0C6F alone points more towards C.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning
Power or charging rate limited
Displayed battery temperatures differ noticeably in live data
c: Sensor C reading off, especially when P0C6F is stored alone
Sensor B reading off, likely when P0C6E is stored as well
Sensor output stuck at one value while the pack temperature changes
Real local heating in a module, for example from a cell with high resistance

P0C70.d: P0C70 is the correlation check between battery temperature sensors C and D. The controller expects both to settle at nearly the same value once the pack has rested, and it stores the code when their difference stays too large.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp or EV system warning
Message asking to plug in or warm the battery
Reduced electric power and slower charging
c: Thermistor C or D drifted out of agreement with the other
Battery control software that sets the code falsely, for example in cold weather
Sensor C or D detached from its cell group
Uneven cooling across the pack, such as a blocked air duct or coolant channel

P0C71.d: P0C71 checks whether battery temperature sensors D and E agree with each other. Both sit in the same pack, so after a long soak they should report almost the same value; a lasting gap means one of them reads wrong although its circuit looks healthy.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Reduced battery charge and discharge power
Battery cooling running more often than usual
c: Thermistor D or E drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor no longer pressed against its cell or module
Genuine temperature difference from uneven cooling or a weak cell group
Battery management software with an overly tight comparison

P0C72.d: P0C72 is the agreement test between battery temperature sensors E and F. The controller stores it when the two readings stay apart by more than a calibrated margin after the pack has had time to even out.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Battery-too-cold or similar message although it is not very cold
Reduced electric power and range
c: Battery module software that reports sensor faults falsely, fixed by reprogramming
Thermistor E or F drifted without an electrical fault
Sensor detached from its cell group
Uneven coolant or air flow through the pack

P0C73.d: P0C73 reports that coolant pump A of the motor electronics, the loop that cools the inverter and often the drive motor, does not run the way the controller commands. Kia's bulletins for Niro and Carnival hybrids use exactly this name.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid warning lamp
Coolant warning in the instrument cluster
Reduced electric drive power at high load
c: Air trapped in the inverter cooling loop, often after coolant service
Water ingress and corrosion at the pump connector or inside the pump housing
Low coolant level, wrong mixture or frozen coolant
Control-unit software with faulty judgement logic

P0C74.d: P0C74 is the performance check for coolant pump B of the motor electronics, found on vehicles with a second electric pump in the power electronics cooling. The controller compares how the pump should run with how it actually runs and stores the code when the two disagree for longer than calibrated.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Reduced electric drive power when the electronics run hot
c: Hybrid control or inverter module software, fixed by an update
Air pocket in the power electronics coolant loop
Pump B worn, blocked or seized
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at pump B

P0C75.d: P0C75 is logged when the high-voltage bus loses its voltage faster than expected after the contactors open. At shutdown the inverter's DC-link capacitor is drained through a discharge resistor or an active discharge circuit, and from capacitance and resistance the controller knows roughly how long that should take.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Vehicle may not become ready to drive
c: DC-link capacitor lost capacitance through ageing or damage
Additional load or leakage path on the high-voltage bus
Bus voltage measured incorrectly by the inverter or battery module
Discharge resistor or circuit with too low a resistance

P0C76.d: P0C76 means the high-voltage bus is still too high a set time after the contactors opened, so the inverter capacitor was not drained as intended. GM publishes thresholds: the 2011 Volt flags more than 200 V after 3.5 s (Special Type C, no MIL), the 2013 eAssist cars more than 65 V after 6.5 s and the 2019 tables more than 200 V after 3.5 s, both Type A after two failed runs.
s: Hybrid warning lamp or service high voltage message
Vehicle may not start or become ready
Loss of propulsion
c: Active discharge circuit or discharge resistor in the inverter failed
Main contactor welded closed so the battery keeps feeding the bus
Loose high-voltage cable or terminal at the inverter
Low 12 V supply during shutdown or module software

P0C77.d: P0C77 is stored when the inverter side reaches battery voltage too quickly during precharge. Before the main contactor closes, the controller charges the inverter capacitor through a precharge resistor and watches the ratio of bus to battery voltage.
s: Malfunction indicator or hybrid warning lamp
Vehicle does not become ready or loses propulsion
c: Main contactor welded or closing before precharge ends
Loose high-voltage cable leaving the inverter capacitor partly disconnected
Faulty bus or battery voltage measurement

P0C78.d: P0C78 means precharge took too long: the inverter side did not come up to battery voltage within the allowed time. GM's 2011 Volt allows 700 ms to reach 95 % (Type A), the 2013 eAssist 1,000 ms or more than 5 A for over 100 ms (Type B), and the 2019 tables demand 95-105 % at 0.700 s, Type A.
s: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Malfunction indicator lamp and drive system message
Loss of propulsion
c: Precharge resistor, precharge contactor or high-voltage fuse open
Faulty high-voltage consumer such as a coolant heater loading the bus
Battery module software, fixed by an update
Loose high-voltage cable or bus bar

P0C79.d: P0C79 reports that the DC voltage at the inverter of drive motor A rose above its protection limit. Overvoltage can come from regenerative energy the battery cannot absorb, from a contactor opening under load or a loose high-voltage connection, and it can also be a false reading.
s: Hybrid or EV warning lamp, electrical system fault message
Drive system will not activate or shuts down until restarted
Reduced drive power
c: Battery cable at the inverter loose or not at specified torque
Inverter or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike from regeneration or a contactor opening under load
Motor control software, fixed by an update

P0C7A.d: P0C7A is the overvoltage code for the inverter of drive motor B, which on many all-wheel-drive hybrids is the rear motor. Mitsubishi documents it for the Outlander PHEV: in the 2018 model the rear motor control unit has a hardware high-voltage switch that closes at 420 V, a higher limit than the 370 V of the front unit, and the code sets after a single trip with the power stage active or after 0.5 s with it switched
s: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Reduced drive power, rear axle drive may be unavailable
c: Rear battery cable connection loose at the rear motor control unit
Rear motor control unit or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike from regeneration or a contactor event

P0C7B.d: P0C7B sets when the inverter of the generator, the motor-generator the engine drives to make electricity, sees DC voltage above its limit. Mitsubishi is the only maker found documenting the code by number: in the 2018 Outlander PHEV the generator control unit trips a hardware high-voltage switch at 370 V, and one occurrence with the power stage running, or 0.5 s with it switched off, is enough.
s: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Engine-driven charging or hybrid drive restricted
c: Front battery cable at the power drive unit not at specified torque
Generator control unit or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike when a contactor opens while the generator charges

P0C7C.d: P0C7C is the umbrella circuit code for battery temperature sensor G, used when the controller sees an electrical fault in that input without sorting it into low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents P0C7C publicly.
s: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp, check-engine lamp on many models
Reduced electric power and slower charging
Battery cooling or heating running without obvious need
c: Corroded or loose connector between sensor G and the sensing board
Faulty input stage on the cell monitoring board or battery module

P0C7D.d: P0C7D flags sensor G when its value is electrically valid but does not fit the rest of the pack. GM's 2012 Volt table (12OBDG01A) compares it with the average of the other sensors once propulsion has been off for more than 21,600 s and fails it beyond 25.3 °C in 50 of 67 samples, Type B with two trips; bulletin 18-NA-342 calls it sensor 7 performance.
s: Check-engine or hybrid warning lamp after a long parking period
Reduced battery power, sometimes a battery-too-cold message
c: Thermistor G drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor G no longer seated against its cell group
Battery module software setting the code falsely (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)
Real temperature difference from a weak cell or blocked cooling channel

P0C7E.d: P0C7E means the sensor G voltage has fallen below its valid range. The thermistor has a negative temperature coefficient and a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground looks like an extremely hot cell group; low describes the signal, not the temperature.
s: Warning lamp with sharply reduced electric power
Battery cooling fan or chiller running constantly
Engine runs more often on plug-in hybrids
c: Sensor G signal line chafed through and shorted to ground
Thermistor G shorted internally, often after moisture entry
Input stage of the cell monitoring board pulled low

P0C7F.d: With P0C7F the sensor G input reads above its valid voltage range. Because the pull-up raises the line when the thermistor is disconnected, an open circuit, broken wire or unplugged connector shows up as an implausibly cold cell group.
s: Battery-too-cold or plug-in-to-warm message although it is not very cold
Reduced electric power or no electric drive
Battery heater switched on without need
c: Open circuit or unplugged connector at sensor G
Module software setting it falsely in mild cold (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)

P0C80.d: P0C80 catches a sensor G signal that jumps around instead of following the slow thermal drift of a large battery. GM spells out the logic in its hybrid tables 18OBDG02 and 19OBDG02: every 100 ms the module sums the absolute changes of the reading across a 10-sample window, a total above 10 fails that window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 set the code as Type B, two trips, provided system voltage exceeds 10.2 V and th
s: Warning lamp that may come and go between trips
Jumping sensor G value in live data
Occasional power reduction
c: Loose or fretting terminal in the sensor G connector
Conductor cracked inside the insulation, breaking under vibration
Cell monitoring board with unstable reference or ground

P0C81.d: P0C81 reports an electrical fault on the input of battery temperature sensor H that the controller does not narrow down further. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly.
s: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Limited acceleration in electric mode
Charging slower than usual
c: Poor contact at the sensor H connector
Damaged measuring channel on the sensing board
